parts.name: full_model
parts.original_hypothesis: Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.729 + linear_backbone + state_offsets + usage_service_nonlinear + minor_hinges), additive in logit; the four children never feed each other. 26 unconnected inputs (24 state one-hots, areaCode:510, totalEveCalls, totalEveCharge, totalIntlMinutes, totalIntlCalls and others) are zero-effect entries. Interpretation: a logistic-regression backbone (international plan +, voicemail plan -, intl charge +, night minutes +), a per-state offset table (exactly linear in the one-hots), and a block of genuine ReLU hinges on day/evening usage and customer-service calls that implements the known churn rules (heavy day usage without voicemail; 4+ service calls, especially with low day usage). Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): AUC 0.908, acc 0.909. Mean-ablation AUC: linear_backbone -> 0.826, usage_service_nonlinear -> 0.709, state_offsets -> 0.902, minor_hinges -> 0.908. Replacing every hidden unit by its least-squares linear fit on its own inputs gives AUC 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843), so essentially all of the gain over a linear model comes from usage_service_nonlinear (Shapley share: heavy usage/service tradeoff 0.029, service calls with low day usage 0.018, day charge without voicemail 0.016, service-call hinge 0.007, day-minutes hinge 0.002). Rare-category effects (net logit, train rows): state:11 -2.14 (73 rows, 3 churners; empirical log-odds offset -1.20), state:4 +2.02 (41 rows; empirical +0.83), state:47 +1.17 (72), state:26 +0.92 (75), state:0 -0.76 (56), state:22 suppresses the low-usage service-call unit (in-state effect -1.97 to +0.98). These are 1.5-2.5x the empirical offsets: candidates for repair. SHAP (300 rows) top: day charge, customer-service calls, international plan, voicemail plan, eve minutes, day minutes (the same column as day charge after z-scoring), intl charge, night minutes, vmail messages, account length.

parts.name: usage_service_nonlinear
parts.original_hypothesis: Additive sum (identity node nl_agg, weight 1) of the five leaves on the continuous usage and service-call inputs. The leaves never feed each other; they are summed in logit. Together they encode the classic churn rules: churn rises sharply with heavy day+evening usage (heavy_usage, day_charge_no_voicemail, day_minutes_hinge) and with 4+ customer-service calls (service_calls_hinge), especially when day usage is low (service_calls_low_day_usage), while heavy users are not penalised again for calls (10992). This block is where the network beats logistic regression: replacing each leaf by its least-squares linear fit on its own entry inputs lowers train AUC from 0.908 to 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843). Shapley split of that 0.072 AUC: heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff 0.029, service_calls_low_day_usage 0.018, day_charge_no_voicemail 0.016, service_calls_hinge 0.007, day_minutes_hinge 0.002. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula; viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.709 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 1.541; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.836.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
